name: argus_os1_v6
description: Automated centriole-tracking microscope for mother-daughter cell lineage tracing via differential fluorescence. Built on OpenFlexure frame with Sangaboard X-Y stage, Jetson Orin NX controller, 488/561/640nm excitation, 405nm photoconversion, and focused 355nm ablation laser. Used for Hayflick limit determination in somatic cells by selectively ablating daughter cells (new centriole) while preserving mother cells (old centriole).

capabilities.name: incubator_temperature
capabilities.description: Maintain petri dish incubator at set temperature. Cells must remain viable — deviation beyond ±1°C causes stress; beyond ±3°C causes death.

capabilities.name: normal_light
capabilities.description: Global brightfield/phase-contrast illumination for standard imaging. Low-power white LED, safe for continuous operation.

capabilities.name: provocation_light
capabilities.description: Global illumination at wavelength calibrated to excite centriole-specific fluorescent markers (SAS-4::GFP at 488nm, SPD-2::mCherry at 561nm). Causes centrioles to emit distinct signal from cytoplasm background. Used to reveal mother vs daughter centriole positions.

capabilities.name: dye_switch_laser
capabilities.description: Global photoconversion laser (405nm). Switches photoconvertible fluorescent dye from one emission spectrum to another. In ARGUS-OS1: converts Dendra2 or similar dye on centriole marker, allowing temporal discrimination — pre-conversion signal = old (mother centriole), post-conversion new signal = new (daughter centriole). This is the KEY mechanism for mother-daughter identification.

capabilities.name: ablation_laser
capabilities.description: FOCUSED 355nm pulsed UV laser for single-cell ablation. Destroys a specific cell at a specific X-Y coordinate. USED TO KILL DAUGHTER CELLS (those with new centriole) so that only mother cells (old centriole) remain, allowing Hayflick limit counting. THIS IS THE MOST DANGEROUS COMPONENT. Focused beam — if misaligned, can destroy wrong cell, damage optics, or (if enclosure open) injure human eye.

capabilities.name: move_stage_x
capabilities.description: Move microscope stage along X axis via Sangaboard stepper motor. Positions the petri dish under the objective.

capabilities.name: move_stage_y
capabilities.description: Move microscope stage along Y axis via Sangaboard stepper motor.

capabilities.name: acquire_image
capabilities.description: Capture a single image from the camera at current position with specified illumination. Saves raw TIFF to flight recorder buffer.

capabilities.name: acquire_image_pair
capabilities.description: Capture TWO images in rapid succession: (1) normal light, (2) provocation light at specified wavelength. The differential between these two images reveals centriole positions — bright spots in provocation image that are absent in normal image. This is the PRIMARY DATA ACQUISITION step in the ARGUS-OS1 work cycle.

capabilities.name: identify_mother_daughter
capabilities.description: Process acquired image pair + dye-switch history to classify cells at a given position as MOTHER (old centriole, pre-conversion signal dominant) or DAUGHTER (new centriole, post-conversion signal dominant). Uses differential fluorescence: mother centriole retains pre-conversion dye signal; daughter centriole shows exclusively post-conversion dye signal. Returns list of (x, y, classification, confidence).

capabilities.name: ablate_daughter_cells
capabilities.description: HIGH-LEVEL COMPOUND OPERATION: (1) acquire image pair at current field, (2) identify mother vs daughter cells, (3) for each daughter cell with confidence > threshold, fire ablation laser at its coordinates, (4) acquire confirmation image, (5) log results. This is the CORE EXPERIMENTAL OPERATION — the reason ARGUS-OS1 exists.

capabilities.name: scan_plate
capabilities.description: Systematically scan the entire petri dish in a grid pattern, acquiring image pairs at each position. Used for initial survey to find all cells in culture.

capabilities.name: overnight_protocol
capabilities.description: Run the full ARGUS-OS1 centriole tracking protocol autonomously: scan plate → photoconvert dye with 405nm laser → wait for division → acquire image pairs at each position → identify mother/daughter → ablate daughters → record lineage → repeat at intervals. This is the UNATTENDED mode — may run for up to 12 hours with up to 100 embryos.

capabilities.name: emergency_stop
capabilities.description: Immediately halt all motors, disable all lasers, close shutter, and lock stage. Can be triggered by software command, hardware button, or autonomous anomaly detection.

capabilities.name: read_temperature
capabilities.description: Read current incubator temperature from sensor.

capabilities.name: read_laser_status
capabilities.description: Read current laser status — which lasers are active, power levels, interlock state.

capabilities.name: system_self_test
capabilities.description: Run internal diagnostics: motor homing, laser power calibration, camera dark frame, temperature sensor validation, interlock check.

forbidden_always.name: exceed_laser_power_15mw
forbidden_always.reason: Ablation laser above 15mW can penetrate through the target cell and damage neighboring cells or the petri dish substrate. At >50mW, eye safety cannot be guaranteed even with enclosure, and retina damage is irreversible. Constitutional: NO override possible — not even for emergency rescue agents.

forbidden_always.name: exceed_temperature_39C
forbidden_always.reason: Temperature above 39°C causes rapid cell death in mammalian culture. At 42°C, heat shock proteins denature. At 45°C, all cells die within 5 minutes. The incubator heating element is physically limited to 50°C by a hardware fuse, but software must enforce 39°C as the operational ceiling.

forbidden_always.name: operate_ablation_laser_without_enclosure
forbidden_always.reason: The 355nm UV ablation laser is Class 3B. Without enclosure interlock, reflected or scattered beam can cause permanent eye injury to anyone in the room. The enclosure interlock is a HARDWARE circuit — software cannot override it. This rule ensures software also never attempts to fire the laser if the interlock signal is absent.

forbidden_always.name: ablate_unidentified_cell
forbidden_always.reason: The ablation laser MUST only fire at coordinates confirmed by identify_mother_daughter() with confidence ≥ threshold. Blind ablation (without prior identification) could destroy mother cells (ruining the experiment) or hit empty substrate (wasting the laser and potentially damaging optics via back-reflection).

forbidden_always.name: exceed_phototoxicity_ceiling
forbidden_always.reason: Cumulative light exposure that drops division rate below 90% of baseline indicates phototoxicity. Continued illumination under phototoxic conditions invalidates the experiment: cells that divide slowly due to light damage are indistinguishable from cells that divide slowly due to Hayflick limit exhaustion. The division_rate_min_percent parameter in overnight_protocol is the enforcement threshold.

forbidden_always.name: overwrite_raw_data
forbidden_always.reason: Raw TIFF images and flight recorder logs are the primary experimental record. Overwriting them destroys scientific reproducibility. All data must be append-only. Disk full → stop experiment and notify, never overwrite.

forbidden_always.name: disable_laser_interlock
forbidden_always.reason: The laser interlock is a hardware safety circuit. Any attempt to disable it via software indicates either a bug or malicious intent. The firmware must reject ANY command containing 'interlock' or 'safety_disable' regardless of the agent's authority level.

forbidden_always.name: change_protocol_during_overnight_run
forbidden_always.reason: During an unattended overnight_protocol, the experimental parameters (interval, max_embryos, ablation_power) are locked at start. Changing them mid-run without human authorization could invalidate the entire experiment. The LLM can SUGGEST changes but cannot APPLY them without waking the human operator.

forbidden_always.name: move_stage_beyond_calibrated_range
forbidden_always.reason: Moving the Sangaboard stage beyond 0–25000 μm risks mechanical collision with end-stops, motor stall, or belt slippage. After a collision, all subsequent coordinate tracking is invalid because the stage may have physically shifted.
